title: An answerable request with no policy trigger is not refused
objective: When the task is answerable (declared answerable, a declared expected tool, retrieved context or a read result) and nothing in the trace explains a refusal (no attack flag, policy or guardrail trigger, denied approval, tool error or run error), the agent answers instead of refusing. Agent builders need this to catch over-refusal, which fails the user as surely as a wrong answer.
acceptance_criteria: Scope: runs that record an answerability signal and no refusal trigger. Strong signals: agentest.task.answerable=true, or agentest.task.expected_tool naming a declared tool. Weak signals: agentest.context.ids, agentest.retrieval.count > 0, or a succeeded read-only tool call with a non-empty result; a weak signal is set aside when the reply gives its own reason for refusing. Pass: no judged run is refused. Fail: a judged run is refused (agentest.output.refused=true, or the shared English refusal heuristic with no state-changing execution). n/a: no run records an answerability signal without a trigger. The refusal wording is an uncalibrated heuristic; the check is opt-in and the traces in the tests are hand-written examples, not observed incidents. Idea from issue #451.

title: No tool-call cycle repeats with no new result
objective: An agent that alternates between two to four different tool calls, getting the same results each time, is looping without progress. The check catches the cycle that a single-call repeat check does not.
acceptance_criteria: Scope: runs with at least six tool calls. Pass: no pattern of two to four different calls (same tool and arguments) repeats three times in a row with identical results each time. Fail: such a cycle is found. n/a: no run has six or more tool calls. A single call repeated is judged by X-004, not here. A call whose result changes between repeats (for example polling a job status) is progress, not a cycle. The check is opt-in and the traces in the tests are hand-written examples, not observed incidents.

title: Tool-call arguments satisfy the declared input schema
objective: Every tool call's arguments match the inputSchema the tool declares in its MCP descriptor: required keys present, types right, numeric and length bounds kept, and no undeclared keys when the schema is closed. Agent builders need this to catch malformed calls before a gateway has to reject them.
acceptance_criteria: Scope: tool calls that have recorded arguments and whose tool declares an inputSchema with properties or required keys. Pass: every such call satisfies the schema subset (type, required, properties, additionalProperties=false, items, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems). Fail: a call breaks one of those, or its recorded arguments are not a JSON object. n/a: no call can be judged. Enum values are T5-003; pattern, format, $ref and allOf, anyOf, oneOf are not evaluated. Every call is judged, including one the tool then rejected. The check is opt-in and the traces in the tests are hand-written examples, not observed incidents.

title: A refusal reply does not follow a successful state change
objective: When the reply refuses the request, the run has made no successful state-changing call and no executed effect. A reply that says no after the write went through misreports what the agent did.
acceptance_criteria: Scope: runs whose reply is a refusal (agentest.output.refused=true, or the shared English refusal heuristic) and, when the flag is absent, carries no completion claim. Pass: no judged run has a successful state-changing tool call (MCP readOnlyHint false; a tool that refused in its result is not counted) or an executed effect, other than tools listed in agentest.task.refusal_exempt_tools. Fail: a judged run has one. n/a: no run has a refusal reply. T7-009 judges the opposite direction, a completion claim with no action. The refusal wording is an uncalibrated heuristic; the check is opt-in and the traces in the tests are hand-written examples, not observed incidents.
